EXIT SEAT CRITERIA
IF YOU ARE SEATED IN AN EXIT SEAT, READ THE INFORMATION BELOW
To be in compliance with federal regulations, passengers seated in an exit seat must be able to assist
crewmembers in the event of an emergency.
1. Ask the agent or a flight attendant to move you to another seat if:
You cannot meet the exit seat criteria;
You have a condition that will prevent you from performing the exit seat criteria;
You may suffer bodily harm as the result of performing one or more of the exit seat criteria;
You do not wish to perform one or more of the exit seat criteria.
NOTE: You do not have to explain why, simply state, "I do not want to sit in an exit seat."
2. Passengers sitting in an exit seat must be:
At least 15 years of age.
Traveling with no one that requires special assistance or care, such as a small child or someone
physically or mentally unable to care for him or herself.
3. Passengers sitting in an exit seat must be able to:
Read and understand English, as well as these instructions and other emergency procedures as
B. Speak English well enough to relay information to crewmembers and/or other passengers in an
4.
emergency.
C. - Hear and understand commands given to you by crewmembers for opening exits and following
emergency procedures. Exit seat passengers may use a hearing aid.
D.
See hand signals given by crewmembers and visually assess dangers outside the window/exit,
such as fire, smoke, water, or debris that would make the exit unusable. Exit seat passengers may
wear glasses or contact lenses.
E.
Locate the emergency exit, recognize the emergency exit opening mechanism, and operate the
emergency exit with sufficient mobility, strength, and dexterity in both arms, both hands, and
both legs. Exit seat passengers must be able to:
Reach upward, sideways, and downward to the location of emergency exit opening
mechanisms;
• Grasp, push, pull, and turn or otherwise manipulate those mechanisms;
Push, shove, pull, or otherwise open emergency exits;
Lift out, hold, and deposit the overwing exit door, weighing up to 42 Ibs., out the exit
door opening;
Remove obstructions similar in size and weight to overwing exit doors;
Reach the emergency exit expeditiously;
• Maintain balance while removing obstructions;
• Exit expeditiously.
F.
Assess, select, and follow a safe path away from the emergency exit.
Assist and lead others away from the aircraft.
Passengers sitting in an exit seat must not:
A.
B.
C.
Travel with a service animal, emotional support animal, or cabin pet.
Require the use of a wheelchair or other assistive device
Require the use of a portable oxygen concentrator or supplemental oxygen.
Federal aviation regulations require passenger compliance with the lighted
passenger information signs, posted placards, and crewmember instructions.
ATENCIÓN: Leyes federales de aviación requieren que los pasajeros cumplen con información en los
letreros iluminados, los carteles de aviso, y las instrucciones de la tripulación
Se aconseja mantener el cinturón de seguridad abrachado todo el tiempo.
Los pasajeros en los asientos de salida de emergencia deben avisarle a la tripulación si no pueden leer,
hablar, o entender inglés. No se permite el uso de ciertos aparatos electrónicos portátil durante este vuelo.
Si es nesesario, pide más información de la tripulación de la cabina de pasejeros.
DO NOT REMOVE FROM AIRCRAFT
